title: macos publish ships a Menuz.app built off the release tag: app-sign builds whatever HEAD is, and publish checks only the bundle id and version
body:
## What

utilz-ic, 23 Oct 2026, reading `bin/devbin macos` before hv's post-cut steps for 2.14.2. vc read the same code and agreed that day, and gave the fix to utilz-ic, to ride the next release.

A release's `Menuz.app.zip` carries the build stamps of whatever tree `app-sign` ran in. `app-sign` builds HEAD, whatever commit that is. `publish` checks only the bundle's id and version. So a Menuz.app built from a commit other than the release tag's ships as that release's asset, and nothing refuses it: not `app-sign`, `app-notarize` or `publish`, and not a Homebrew install's `menuz install`. In every Homebrew install, the menu's top row then names that commit and the kind `dev`, and the bundle can carry code that is not the tag's. 2.14.2's first publish did exactly this (Measured).

## Measured

23 Oct 2026, after 2.14.2's cut (tag `2.14.2` on `54b6262d`).

- `cmd_app_sign` (`bin/.devbin/cmd/macos:373` to `:405`) builds through `"$ROOT/bin/utilz" menuz build --release`. It reads nothing of HEAD or the tag. `ROOT` is the tree the script sits in (`bin/devbin:45`).
- menuz stamps a build from HEAD (`opt/menuz/menuz:570` to `:608`), and the bundle carries the stamps as `MenuzCommit`, `CFBundleVersion` and `MenuzKind`:
  - `MENUZ_COMMIT` is HEAD's first eight characters, and `MENUZ_BUILD` is HEAD's commit count.
  - `MENUZ_KIND` is `release` only when `git tag --points-at HEAD` names the root `VERSION`'s tag and the source stamp is clean. Otherwise it is `dev`.
- `app_ship_blockers` (`cmd/macos:333` to `:342`) reads only `CFBundleIdentifier`, and `CFBundleShortVersionString` against `opt/menuz/VERSION`. It is the one check `publish` runs on the bundle itself, on the staged copy (`:488`) and again on the copy unpacked from the zip (`:507`).
- A Homebrew install's `fetch_asset` (`opt/menuz/menuz:826` to `:864`) checks the asset's signature, `spctl`'s `source=Notarized Developer ID`, its bundle id and its version. It checks nothing of its kind or its commit.
- `help/menuz.md:264` says the signed release asset is built at the tag from a clean tree, so a Homebrew install's app shows the release form. `docs/releasing.md:70` has hv run the three steps "at the tag". Nothing checks either.
- After the cut, the nodes' whiteboard records moved main past the tag: at `4e6dd63b`, five commits past it, `git tag --points-at HEAD` printed nothing. Then it happened:
  - hv's first pass ran `app-sign`, `app-notarize` and `publish`, chained, in the primary at `98651ed1`, before ic's note reached hv.
  - At 20:13:28Z release 2.14.2 took a `Menuz.app.zip` with sha256 `bfbef75dd697`: menuz 0.4.7, build 1693, `MenuzCommit 98651ed1`, `MenuzKind dev`, signed and notarised. `publish` passed it. (vc's read of the asset.)
  - ic read the bundle that pass left at `~/.local/state/menuz/build/macos/dist/Menuz.app`, its `Info.plist` written at 20:12:52Z: 0.4.7, 1693, `98651ed1`, `dev`. The tag's build is 1687, `54b6262d`, `release`.
  - hv deleted the asset, and ic read the release with no assets at 20:15Z. hv then rebuilt from a detached worktree at the tag (vc's `~/Devel/scratch/utilz-vc/wt-2142`), whose `xcodebuild` ran with `MENUZ_BUILD=1687`, `MENUZ_COMMIT=54b6262d` and `MENUZ_KIND=release`.
  - The tap was not yet pushed, so no Homebrew install fetched the dev asset (vc).
- Before 2.14.2, no asset built off its tag had shipped:
  - 2.14.1's `Menuz.app.zip` reads 0.4.5, build 1425, `MenuzCommit 43fca620`, `MenuzKind release`.
  - 2.14.0's reads 0.1.0, build 1214, `069e0f38`, `release`.
  - Each is its tag's commit and count.

## Fix

1. `publish` refuses a bundle, uploading nothing, when its `MenuzKind` is not `release`, or its `MenuzCommit` is not the first eight characters of the commit the root `VERSION`'s tag names. It checks the staged bundle and the bundle unpacked from the zip, as it refuses a wrong version today. Each refusal names the value it read and the one it wanted. A tag that does not exist in the tree is refused by name.
2. `app-sign` refuses before any build when HEAD does not carry the root `VERSION`'s tag. The refusal names HEAD, the tag and the commit the tag names, so the build and the signing are never spent on a bundle `publish` would refuse. Whether `app-sign` refuses or only warns is for vc's read of the design.
3. `docs/releasing.md`'s "After every cut, at the tag" says how to run the three steps: in a tree whose HEAD is the tag, which is a detached worktree once main has moved past it. It also says `app-sign` and `publish` refuse otherwise. `bin/devbin macos`'s own help names the new refusals.
4. Tests in `opt/menuz/test/macos.bats` sit beside `publish`'s refusals. A bundle stamped `dev`, and one whose commit is not the tag's, are each refused with nothing uploaded. `app-sign` refuses off the tag before any build. The existing pass case is stamped as the tag's build.
5. Not here unless vc's read adds it: `menuz install` refusing an asset whose `MenuzKind` is not `release`, as a check a Homebrew install makes for itself.

## Design

utilz-ic, 23 Oct 2026, for vc's read before any code. Size S.

1. **One answer to "may this bundle ship with this release".** `app_ship_blockers` (`cmd/macos:333`) already answers it for the bundle id and the version, and `publish` asks it twice: of the staged bundle, and of the bundle unpacked from the zip. It takes the release tag as a second argument, the one `publish` already reads from `VERSION` (`:487`). It gains two reasons, so both of `publish`'s calls get them and no call is added:
   - `MenuzKind` is not `release`: `the bundle's MenuzKind is dev, not release -- it was built off the tag 2.14.2 or from a dirty tree; run app-sign and app-notarize in a tree at the tag`.
   - `MenuzCommit` is not the tag's:
     - The full commit the tag names is read with `git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify --quiet "refs/tags/$tag^{commit}"`. It must begin with the bundle's `MenuzCommit`, which must be eight characters or more.
     - The refusal reads `the bundle's MenuzCommit is 98651ed1 and the tag 2.14.2 names 54b6262d -- ...`.
     - Comparing by prefix holds whatever length `--short=8` gave at the build.
   - A tag that is not in the tree is a reason of its own, `the tag 2.14.2 that VERSION names is not in this tree, so the bundle's commit cannot be checked against it`, rather than a commit that cannot match.
2. **app-sign refuses off the tag, before the build, on menuz's own answer.** menuz's `build_kind` (`opt/menuz/menuz:589` to `:608`) is the one place that decides whether a build is the release's, so app-sign asks it rather than reading the tags itself.
   - Just before the build step, app-sign runs `"$ROOT/bin/utilz" menuz stamps`, which prints what the next build will carry, and refuses unless it says `MENUZ_KIND=release`.
   - The refusal names `MENUZ_COMMIT` and `MENUZ_KIND`, the tag `VERSION` names and the commit that tag names (point 1's read, one helper for both), and the worktree command.
   - A `menuz stamps` that fails stops app-sign, naming it.
   - It refuses rather than warns: a Developer ID signature and a notary submission are for the release asset alone, and every other build is `menuz build`'s.
   - The check comes after the identity and entitlements checks, so their tests keep their order.
3. **The readback says what it signed.** `app_signature_readback` (`:278`), which app-sign, app-notarize and app-verify all print, adds the bundle's version, build, commit and kind under its identifier, team and flags. hv and vc then read the stamps off the bytes at each step without PlistBuddy. It only reads them: point 1's refusal is publish's and point 2's is app-sign's. This is the one point beyond the Fix, and it is vc's call.
4. **Tests** in `opt/menuz/test/macos.bats`:
   - The fixture project becomes a git repository with one commit tagged `2.14.0`, which is the fixture's `VERSION`. It runs under the test helper's git isolation (`no_git_signing`), and the commit is made with a fixture identity.
   - The fake `bin/utilz` answers `menuz stamps` with the fixture HEAD's commit and `release`, or `$FAKES/stamps.kind` when set.
   - Its `menuz build --release` writes `MenuzCommit` and `MenuzKind` into the bundle's `Info.plist`, from `$FAKES/build.commit` and `$FAKES/build.kind` when set. So the bundles every existing test builds are the tag's.
   - New tests:
     - app-sign refuses, building and signing nothing, when the stamps say `dev`.
     - publish refuses, uploading nothing, a bundle stamped `dev`, a bundle whose commit is not the tag's, and a bundle whose tag is not in the tree.
     - Each refusal's text names what it read and what it wanted.
     - The pass case asserts the readback's new lines.
5. **Proofs,** one at a time, each restored and its bytes' hash checked against G's:
   - R runs the new tests on main's code, each red.
   - G runs the file green.
   - M1 drops the kind reason, and the dev test turns red.
   - M2 drops the commit reason, and the commit test turns red.
   - M3 drops app-sign's check, and its test turns red.
6. **Docs.**
   - `docs/releasing.md:70` says the three steps run in a tree whose HEAD is the tag. After the nodes' records, that is a detached worktree: `git worktree add --detach <dir> <tag>`, the steps run from `<dir>/bin/devbin`, then `git worktree remove <dir>`. It also says app-sign and publish refuse anything else. Its steps 1 and 3 name the new refusals.
   - `bin/devbin macos`'s usage says the same, in a line each.
   - A CHANGELOG line goes under the next open section, whose number is hv's.
7. **Runs,** booked with vc:
   - shellcheck 0.9.0 on `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos` and `macos.bats`, and critic-shell on the diff, before the slot's START.
   - One light slot, with fakes and temp dirs only (no build, GUI, daemon or port): R, G and M1 to M3 with `bats opt/menuz/test/macos.bats`, then `utilz test menuz`.
   - utilz-dc's kovacs leg of `utilz test menuz` on G's bytes, since `tests.yml`'s Ubuntu loop runs `macos.bats` with its fakes.
8. **Not here:** `menuz install` refusing an asset whose kind is not `release` (Fix point 5), unless vc's read adds it. It would be a check in `fetch_asset` (`opt/menuz/menuz:826`) beside the version's, with a test in `menuz.bats`.
